thread:
IncidentBot: P1 — elevated 95th/99th latency for embeddings + small-model generate in us-west1 starting now. Affected endpoint: /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate. Paging: @priya

priya: Im on it. seeing 95p latency jump from ~120ms to ~900ms across several pools. No spike in error rate yet.

alex: pulling perf dashboards. QPS steady, but token-level inflight increased and KV cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 20% in last 8m.

maria: any deploys? I see a config change to cache strategy rolled 04:30 UTC (kv-cache-mode: aggressive). @sam did that land in runtime?

sam: yes, we promoted a cache rewrite (kv-cache aggressive eviction) in rtn-cache-2.0 at 04:28. It switches from LRU to shard-based aggressive eviction to free memory faster. We tested microbenchmarks but not long-tail embed workloads.

jonathan: aggressive eviction could cause cold-starts and cache thrash on popular prefixes, raising end-to-end latency. Can we toggle the legacy cache mode quickly?

priya: attempting toggle to 'stable' mode on the pool. `infractl runtime config set --pool=emb-uw1 --kv-cache-mode=stable --reason="incident rollback"`

IncidentBot: Config change submitted. Applying to 10% of nodes for canary.

elena: drafting status update. Proposed short: "Increased tail latency for Embeddings and Small-Model Generation in us-west1 due to a cache policy regression. Were reverting the policy and monitoring. Some requests may experience slow responses (high 95th/99th)."

priya: canary flip applied. Observing canary nodes: kv hit ratio rising back to ~88% and 95p latency down to ~150ms.

rachel: going to notify top 10 customers active in us-west1. Quick note:

```
Hi <CustomerName>,

Were investigating elevated latency for Embeddings and Generation in us-west1. We have reverted a cache policy change that appears to be the cause and are monitoring. You may see intermittent slow responses for a short period. Well follow up with a summary when we have the full timeline.

Redwood Inference Support
```

alex: good. rolling revert to 100% now in waves (10%->30%->100%) with 3m health checks.

(20 minutes pass)

IncidentBot: Revert to stable kv-cache mode completed to 100% at 05:10 UTC.

priya: Observed system-wide kv hit ratio restored to ~91%. 95p latency trending to baseline 130ms.

sam: root cause confirmed: the shard-based aggressive eviction policy had a bug where hot keys were assigned inconsistent shard ids under some hash seeds, causing frequent cross-shard evictions and effective cache size reduction ~60%. Fix is in PR https://git.redwood/cache/pull/982. Rolling back until we add stronger long-tail workload tests.

jonathan: good catch. For next steps we should: 1) add long-tail embedding/seq benchmarks to the cache test harness, 2) include production-like hash seeds in canary tests, 3) add an alert for sudden drop in kv hit ratio and correlated tail latency. Ill own those action items.

elena: updating status page to Resolved (partial) and adding post-incident follow-up note: short RCA + immediate mitigations + planned preventatives. Draft: 

```
Status: Resolved (partial)
Start: 2026-03-12 04:36 UTC
End: 2026-03-12 05:10 UTC
Impact: Elevated tail latency for Embeddings and Small-Model Generation in us-west1. Some customer requests experienced slow responses.
Cause: regression in new kv-cache eviction policy causing cache thrash and effective cache-size reduction.
Mitigation: reverted kv-cache mode to stable, staged rollback completed. Monitoring shows latency returned to baseline.
Next steps: additional regression tests, stronger canary randomness coverage, alerts for kv hit ratio drops.
```

priya: sending targeted customer notes now and linking status page.

rachel: queued customer DM for top impacted accounts. Also marking follow-up: offer to review logs for any customer who requests deeper impact analysis.

sam: PR includes test that simulates hot prefixes and uses production hash seeds. Ill not re-roll until tests pass.

jonathan: creating infra ticket INFRA-1270 to add kv-hit-ratio alert and correlate with per-route tail latency.

elena: preparing customer-facing post-incident email. Draft below: 

```
Subject: Follow-up: Increased latency for Embeddings/Generation in us-west1 (Mar 12)

Hi <CustomerName>,

Were following up about increased latency you may have seen for Embeddings and Small-Model Generation requests originating in us-west1 on Mar 12.

Summary: A recently deployed cache policy change intended to improve memory reclamation caused unexpected cache thrashing for certain hot workloads, which increased tail latency. We reverted the change and restored baseline performance within ~34 minutes.

What we did: Reverted the cache policy across affected nodes, performed canary validation, and monitored system metrics until hit ratios and latency returned to baseline.

Preventative actions:
- Expand cache regression tests to include long-tail/hot-prefix workloads and production hash seeds.
- Strengthen canary validation to include kv-hit-ratio and 95/99 latency thresholds.
- Add alerts for sudden kv hit ratio drops and queue/backlog signals.
- Coordinate rollout windows and increase rollout conservatism for cache-config changes.

If you noticed user-facing impact wed be happy to review request traces for you. Reply to this message and well escalate.

Thanks for your patience,
Redwood Inference Support
```

priya: looks good. scheduling send to impacted list in 30m.

elena: internal postmortem notes: timeline, PR links, customer comms link, and owner assignments. Ill post a full PMR in #postmortems tomorrow with attachments.

sam: BTW, we also discovered a missing exception path that made the eviction counter reset under heavy concurrent writes. It would have resurfaced if we had had 10x the write QPS; adding that fix to the PR as well.

jonathan: assigning preventatives to owners: cache-tests -> sam, alerts -> infra@team, canary-safeguards -> platform@team.

priya: marking incident closed in channel. Incident resolved at 05:10 UTC. Thanks all for quick response. :white_check_mark:

elena: great work. Ill follow up with the short exec summary for customers who want just 2-3 bullets.

alex: extra note for oncall handoff template: include recent cache config diffs and kv-hit-ratio graphs for easier triage. Adding to oncall playbook.

priya: handing off remaining watchers to alex for the afternoon window. Im off now.

alex: taking follow-up ownership. Will watch alerts for next 12h.

IncidentBot: Incident thread closed by priya at 05:15 UTC.
